analysis:
The PR contains only docs and changelog files. It describes provider-side code (ProviderLoop+Serve.swift, CoordinatorClient) that is not in the diff, so the implementation could not be reviewed.

Security-relevant claims:
1. Protocol-1 endpoint-custody responses on same-process reconnect. The provider answers a fresh per-socket nonce with the in-memory X25519 key and does no Apple work. A matching platform could resume authorization from retained evidence. Related threats: T-053, T-054, TB-011, A-003, A-016. The nonce domain separation, the lifetime non-extension guarantee and the revocation checks live elsewhere and are unverified.
2. attestation.md (head ~106) points to an external platform commit saying missing receipt/risk evidence no longer clears a basic grant. It only withholds reward and MDM-removal readiness. This conflicts with the in-repo reference/provider-authorization.md, which attestation.md lines 10 and 19 still cite, and with the threat-model assumptions in T-052/T-055.
3. The changelog says `darkbloom logout` now drains the provider and attempts token revocation, reporting unconfirmed remote revocation. This is positive for A-008 and was not independently verifiable.
4. The changelog adds an opt-in signed-app diagnostic that runs real Apple verification in isolation. Its code is not visible.

Integration should check the actual coordinator and provider code for resumption nonce binding and for whether the receipt-gating relaxation is live.

findings.detail: The rewritten Context paragraph says missing receipt/risk evidence "does not clear an accepted, otherwise valid basic grant". Receipt/risk checks now apply only to rewards and MDM-removal readiness, and the page points to an external platform commit. The base text, and the unchanged line 10 and line 19 of this page, still defer to the in-repo reference/provider-authorization.md. That reference required a verified current risk receipt and complete metric before any grant. The architecture docs now disagree with each other and the canonical threat model (TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-055). Reviewers and operators cannot tell whether a provider with an unverified or missing receipt can serve public traffic. If this describes real behavior, the receipt gate is no longer a serving control: a provider whose receipt lapses, or one that never obtains a risk metric, keeps serving until the proof or policy deadline. Fix: update the threat model and in-repo provider-authorization.md together, state which revision is authoritative, and record the receipt-gating change as a residual risk in T-052/T-053/T-055.
findings.title: Docs weaken the serving-authorization precondition and diverge from the repo's own policy reference

findings.detail:
The new protocol-1 endpoint-custody response answers a coordinator-supplied nonce inside CoordinatorClient, using the process X25519 key. It does no Apple work. Docs say a matching platform can combine it with retained evidence to resume authorization after a same-process reconnect. Nothing in TB-002, TB-011, T-053 or A-003 covers this path. Risks:
- Custody of the X25519 key does not by itself prove Apple App Attest credential, build or SIP state. A replaced or modified process, or a compromised or colluding operator, could resume a grant without a fresh assertion.
- The key becomes a response oracle for any nonce the coordinator sends. The domain separation and origin binding are not shown.
- Resumption could extend effective authorization beyond the original proof validity if the platform implementation is wrong.
The docs only say the platform "must preserve original proof deadlines" and re-check revocation, so this is an unenforced assumption. Fix: add the threat and its mitigations to the model (domain-separated nonce, binding to connection, endpoint and policy generation, no lifetime extension, revocation checked at resume and at every final handoff). Add a coordinator-side test.
findings.title: Endpoint-resumption custody response is new attack surface not covered by the threat model
